chosen.premise: Alakazam psychically creates each spoon, and every one is said to be unique in the entire world.
chosen.hook: Alakazam doesn’t carry ordinary spoons—it makes one-of-one originals.
chosen.visualIdea: Reveal two glowing spoons, label each as a unique original, then show Alakazam gifting one only to someone trusted.
chosen.note: An unusually specific Alakazam-only rule: its spoons are psychically made, individually unique, and potentially gifted only through deep trust. Every part of the premise is directly supported and highly visual.

candidates.premise: Alakazam is the final evolution, but Kadabra only reaches it through a trade—not by leveling up.
candidates.hook: The smartest Pokémon in the room needs another player to evolve.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Abra leveling into Kadabra, then a trade screen transforming Kadabra into Alakazam.
candidates.note: A Pokémon-specific evolution constraint with a clear gameplay rule. The hook is strong, though trade evolution is familiar to many fans.

candidates.premise: Mega Alakazam becomes shorter at 1.2 meters but keeps exactly the same 48-kilogram weight.
candidates.hook: Mega Evolution makes Alakazam shorter—but not lighter.
candidates.visualIdea: Place regular and Mega Alakazam side by side with height and weight labels visibly comparing them.
candidates.note: The exact height-and-weight contradiction is concrete and easy to display. It is compelling, although the comparison depends on the Mega variety data rather than a Pokédex narrative detail.

candidates.premise: Alakazam’s brain grows until death, making its head heavier while its psychic power gets stronger.
candidates.hook: Alakazam’s biggest weakness is also what makes it stronger.
candidates.visualIdea: Age Alakazam across stages as its head enlarges, then connect head weight to rising psychic power.
candidates.note: Highly distinctive lore and excellent visual progression. The cited entries support the growing, heavier head and stronger psychic power, but “biggest weakness” is an interpretation rather than a directly stated fact.

candidates.premise: Alakazam’s muscles are so weak that it uses psychic power just to move its own body.
candidates.hook: Alakazam is powerful enough to fight—but too weak to move normally.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Alakazam struggling with physical movement before psychic energy lifts and propels its body.
candidates.note: The contradiction between immense psychic power and physically weak muscles is well supported. The visual is clear, but the idea is slightly less distinctive than the spoon rule.

candidates.premise: Closing both eyes heightens Alakazam’s other senses, letting it push its abilities to their extremes.
candidates.hook: Alakazam gets stronger by closing both eyes.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Alakazam shutting its eyes as surrounding sound, motion, and psychic signals intensify.
candidates.note: A clean, surprising mechanic directly stated in the Pokédex. The visual can show sensory amplification, but naming or depicting specific heightened senses would go beyond the cited evidence.

rounds.request: N/A—the selected angle is strong enough. Stronger alternatives would need an equally specific Alakazam-only rule or contradiction, direct multi-entry support, and a visual transformation that can be understood immediately.
